DILG BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph s. 2024 OPINION NO. HON. CLIVE D. QUINO Vice-Governor Province of Bukidnon Cloigarcia08@gmaiI.com Dear Vice Gov. Quiöo: This refers to your email dated 07 March 2024, which was forwarded by our Regional Office in Northern Mindanao to the DILG-CentraI Office, regarding your request for guidance on the proposed amendment in the Internal Rules of Procedure on allowing women sangguniang panlalawigan members to act as a presiding officer during the month of March in every year (in celebration of the intemational women's month), and in adoption to the customary practice of the House of Representatives that allows women legislators to preside proceedings during the same month. At the outset, we deem it proper to highlight Sec. 49 of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991" (LGC) as amended, to wit. SECTION 49. Presiding Officer. — (a) The vice-governor shall be the presiding officer Of the sangguniang panlalawigan; the city vice-mayor, Of the sangguniang panlungsod; the municipal vice-mayor of the sangguniang bayan; and the punong barangay, of the sangguniang barangay. The presiding officer shall vote only to break a tie. (b) In the event of the inability of the regular presiding officer to preside at a sanggunian session, the members present and constituting a quorum shall elect from among themselves a temporary presiding officer. He shall certify within ten (IO) days from the passage of ordinances enacted and resolutions adopted by the sanggunian in the session over which he temporarily presided. As can be gleaned from the above-quoted provision, there are two (2) kinds of Presiding Officers contemplated on the afore-quoted provision of the LGC, namely, the (1) the regular presiding officer, and (2) the temporary presiding officer. Moreover, DILG Opinion No. 27, Series of 2016, is instructive on the matter, viz.: The Vice-Governor shall be the regular presiding officer Of theSangguniang Panlalawigan, the city vice-mayor with regard to to the Sangguniang panlungsod, the Municipal Vice-Mayor with regard to the Sangguniang bayan, and the punong barangay with regard to the sangguniang barangay. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

In the event of the inability of the regular presiding officer to preside at a Sanggunian session, the members present and constituting a quorum shall elect from among themselves a temporary presiding officer. Since this procedure is expressly governed by the LGC, the adopted Internal Rules of Procedure (IRP) of the sanggunian cannot in any way, alter, modify, or amend this requirement. Section 49(b) of the LGC must always prevail over that of the IRP" In view of the foregoing, while the intention of the proposed amendment to the sangguniang panlalawigan's IRP is noble, however, it would not be legally feasible without running counter with Section 49(a) and (b) of the LGC, notwithstanding the fact that the premise of introducing such proposal was anchored on the customary practice of the House of Representatives (HOR) insofar as allowing lady legislators to preside on sessions during the month of March of each year. In this regard, we deem it proper to stress that the HOR (as one of the houses in the legislative body), under Section 16(3) of Article VI of the 1987 Constitution of the Philippines, is allowed to determine the rules of its proceedings. As a constitutional creation, the HOR is constitutionally allowed to promulgate its own rules. On the other hand, the local legislative power of local government units, is a statutory grant, and is only granted subordinate legislation, or delegated legislative powers conferred on them by Congress as the national lawmaking body. The delegate cannot be superior to the principal or exercise powers higher than those of the latter 1. Further, while we recognize the Sanggunian's authority under Section 50 of the LGC to adopt its own IRP, however, the same should not be contrary to law nor the constitution, to be valid. In this Department's Opinion No. 76, series of 2007, it has been opined that: The sources of Parliamentary Rules of Procedure of a Sanggunian, as a legislative body, are arranged in the order of hierarchy, to wit: (I) the 1987 Constitution; (2) the Local Government Code; (3) Judicial Decisions; and (4) Adopted Internal Rules of Procedure of the Sanggunian; (5) Parliamentary Practice; (6) Parliamentary Authors; and (7) Customs and Usage. When we say "arranged in the order of hierarchy", we mean that the higher source shall take precedence over the lower source. In other words, lower source can only be applied in the absence of higher source. Accordingly, considering that the LGC itself specifically intended the Vice-Governor to be the regular presiding officer of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, and only in case of inability that the temporary presiding officer will have to take his/her stead in presiding the session, the same should be upheld by the very august body required to give life and spirit of the said provision in the LGC. Be that as it may, may we recommend, however, that in order to retain the august body's due regard to the role of women, especially on women's month, that the said proposal be revisited and rather, advocate that women be given preference in the election of a temporary presiding officer only in the absence or inability of the regular presiding officer to preside the sanggunian's session, and not necessarily intend for ' Magtajas v. Pryce Properties corp. Inc. (G.R. NO. 111097, 20 July 1994, 234 SCRA 255). Page 2 of 3

the regular presiding officer to voluntarily relinquish his/her seat for that purpose (despite absence of any legal or physical impediment on his/her part), for that would unnecessarily expose the regular presiding officer to an administrative liability for failure to do a positive duty required by law for him/her to discharge. Notwithstanding, this opinion shall be without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Thank you.
